author: gbolahan
content:
I was exploring a design that exploits the near-100% redundancy of validators in the beacon state storage.

A sort of validators sector, with structural sharing

https://dev.to/galadd/cutting-beacon-state-storage-by-97-validator-sectors-with-structural-sharing-3p5c

author: gbolahan
content: Kindly give it a read, and let me know what you think of the approach

author: potuz
content: So is the main realization here that deposits come mostly in large batches?

author: gbolahan
content: No, but that if you take 2 full beacon states validators, depending on the time between them, nothing really changes between them. As little as ~0.01%. Wasteful to then have checkpoints for archival storage with that much redundancy (technically almost 100%)

author: tersec
content: Nimbus has done at least part of this (haven't checked all), the refactoring out of the immutable parts of the validators, going back to ... Altair? Bellatrix?

author: tersec
content: rather than storing them in each state

author: gbolahan
content: Yes, the idea is that main storage is separate from how we point to that storage. It doesn't matter the phase, so it goes back to them. I'll check out how Nimbus goes about it

author: gbolahan
content: All that will be stored in each state will be a list of "pointers"

author: potuz
content: Yeah but this is already exploited in clients for storage

author: potuz
content: At least Prysm and Lighthouse already ship state diffs. But we don't exploit the clustering of deposits

author: gbolahan
content: That's nice. I'll take some time to check all out

author: potuz
content: Deposits usually come in batches, pools make large deposits at once. This means there are long stretches with not that many changes on the validator slice and then suddenly we get periods with a lot of new entries. I thought  you meant to exploit this situation for better storage

author: gbolahan
content:
I did see clusters of changes in my data, but my assumption was that that is solved by having 64 validators per chunk. (not necessarily solved. just that it means it favors my design).

But now, upon closer inspection, maybe there's something to actually look into here. Will think about it.
